chapter: Dizzy, Chano Pozo and Afro-Cuban jazz
title: Rhythmic integration problems with Chano
summary: Chano could not communicate in English, so the two rhythms were separate.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: The thing I noticed, and you touched on it earlier -- I'm just talking about recordings, obviously, although I do have some live recordings made in Paris in 1948 when they recorded (inaudible) At the Salle Pleyel Concert, I noticed that in the early -- even with Bauza (inaudible), I imagine because the -- of the two different rhythmic contexts, Wouldn't You, for instance, which was one of his first recordings, first after Cuban recordings -- the first was just about a month after the Town Hall concert -- you get sections where basically the band is playing 4/4, and also it's kind of tupp-tupp-tupp-tooka-tin. And then there are sections where the band pretty much quits and Bauza plays.
The change in the rhythm was here.

No, that's a separate -- that's a separate (inaudible), because, see, if Chano the Channel was able to speak the language then, then the whole thing would be completly different, because then he would have been able to talk to them and teach them exactly how to (inaudible) to this.

But at first he couldn't relate to them, and they couldn't relate to him. And everybody was confused and think somebody (inaudible), because I used to get complaints, said, but we cannot play with that guy banging on that bongo. They throw us off. They couldn't find the beat. Every time they hear something against the beat, they go out on A Limb around -- they're used to so much of that boom, boom, boom, boom, they couldn't communicate.

And that was exactly what Dizzy was looking for the (inaudible). So they -- little by little they begin to get a little more, more, more into the thing. Now, you call practically any (inaudible), and everybody fall in -- don't bother nobody now.
But in those days that was the beginning of the (inaudible).
